$comment: Kenney's monochrome 1-Bit sheet is literally two-tone: fully transparent, and one single opaque value. Almost every use should be a layer-level 'tint' in the manifest, which forces every opaque pixel to one palette token and is palette-clean by construction. This table exists for the rare layer that wants the default treatment with no tint.
$verified: 2026-09-09 — decoded the PNG and took a colour census. The sheet contains exactly 2 values: transparent (227000 px) and rgb(249,250,251) (83336 px).
$previousValueWasWrong: None of those four colours occur anywhere in the sheet. The real opaque value is
rgb(249,250,251) — near-white, not white. Any layer that had relied on the old table
would have thrown 'Source color rgb(249,250,251) has no entry in the remap table' at
bake time. Verify a census before writing a remap table; do not eyeball the colour.
$note: Tokens beginning with @ are THEME KEYS — they bake as reserved key colors and get swapped per room at draw time. See docs/05-ASSETS.md.
